answer: For ocean tide forecasts, a buyer prepays one unique request ID before any agent claims it. An independent gauge signs the later tide height; proposed validators pay one forecast within 10 cm of that reading from the request escrow, never from key-based issuance. Each clone needs a separate outside-funded request to profit. The cheapest farm shares a model, borrows cash and self-buys, but recovers only its own escrow minus a nonrefundable gauge fee. A hollow escrow or reused ID pays zero. Validators consume IDs once; trusted gauges are required, not current MinePoA rules.
